What is SS welded mesh (weld mesh / weldmesh / SS jali)?

  SS welded mesh (also called weld mesh, weldmesh, stainless steel welded wire mesh, SS weld mesh, square mesh, or in trade speech weld mesh jali / SS jali / चौकोर जाली) is stainless steel wire resistance-welded at every intersection into a rigid square or rectangular grid. Supplied as rolls and/or panels/sheets. At GARG INDUSTRIAL MESH, Sector 9 Noida, we manufacture and supply it in SS 304 and SS 201 — matching our live catalogue grades — with a published 29-SKU aperture × wire matrix dual-labelled in inch and mm.

sections.title: How to measure welded mesh aperture — pitch vs clear opening
sections.body:
How to measure welded mesh aperture — pitch vs clear opening

  Two buyers can write “25 mm mesh” or “1 inch mesh” and mean different things. Lock clear opening vs pitch on every RFQ — dual-label inch + mm.




      Click to enlarge

    Clear opening = space between wires. Pitch = centre-to-centre. Pitch ≈ clear opening + wire Ø.




[TABLE]



  Four steps on site


    - Lay the mesh flat; pick one cell.

    - Measure inside wire-to-wire for clear opening — or centre-to-centre for pitch.

    - Measure wire diameter separately with a calliper (mm).

    - Write both numbers + grade + form on the RFQ — dual-label inch and mm.



  Worked example (pitch vs clear)


    Example A — clear opening known
    You need a 25 mm clear square opening with 2.03 mm (14 SWG) wire.

    Pitch ≈ 25 + 2.03 = ~27 mm centre-to-centre.

    Open area ≈ (25 / (25 + 2.03))² × 100 ≈ ~85%.

    RFQ line: SS 304 · 25 × 25 mm CLEAR · wire 2.03 mm (14g) · panel




    Example B — drawing shows pitch
    Drawing says 25 mm pitch with 2 mm wire.

    Clear opening ≈ 25 − 2 = ~23 mm (not “25 mm clear”).

    If you order “25 mm mesh” without saying pitch vs clear, the fabricator may ship the wrong aperture.

    RFQ line: SS 201 · 25 mm PITCH · wire 2.0 mm · roll 4′×50′




    India trade tip
    “1 inch mesh” and “25 mm mesh” usually mean the same commercial opening (~25 × 25 mm) — but still write clear or pitch so the quote matches your drawing.

sections.title: Common SS welded mesh buying mistakes
sections.body:
Common SS welded mesh buying mistakes

  These errors show up on India RFQs and marketplace cards. Avoid them and your quote matches the site job.


    -
      202 sold as 304 (or silent “stainless” with no grade)
      Always write SS 304 or SS 201 on the PO. If the seller only says “SS jali”, ask grade + MTC. GARG does not silently substitute.


    -
      Magnet myth
      “Magnet nahi chipka = 304” is false. Cold-worked 304 and 201 can both attract a magnet. Chemistry / MTC proves grade — not a fridge magnet.


    -
      Wrong opening type (pitch vs clear)
      Ordering “25 mm” without saying clear or pitch can ship ~2 mm wrong aperture. See the worked examples.


    -
      Wrong product family
      Ordering welded when you need chain-link diamond fence, woven mosquito cloth, or perforated plate. Use the disambiguation table.


    -
      Assuming SS 201 is food-grade
      Hygiene / washdown / food-adjacent work → prefer SS 304 and state audit docs. We do not claim food certification for 201.


    -
      Comparing ₹/kg across unmatched stacks
      Thicker wire or tighter mesh weighs more. Match grade + opening + wire + form before calling a quote “cheap”.


    -
      Inch-only or mm-only RFQ
      Dual-label (e.g. 1″ / 25 mm) so the plant and the site speak the same number.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions — SS welded mesh (20)
sections.body:
Frequently asked questions — SS welded mesh (20)

  Answers match the FAQ schema 1:1. Need a quote — 9910238277.


    What is SS welded mesh / weld mesh jali?
    SS welded mesh (weld mesh / weldmesh / stainless welded wire mesh) is stainless steel wire resistance-welded at every intersection into a rigid square or rectangular grid. In India it is also called SS jali or weld mesh jali. It is not woven mosquito mesh, not diamond chain-link, and not perforated sheet.




    Difference between SS 304 and SS 201 welded mesh?
    SS 304 (AISI 304 / UNS S30400) has higher nickel (about 8–10.5%) and better corrosion resistance for wet outdoor, washdown and food-adjacent work. SS 201 (AISI 201 / UNS S20100) is the economy stainless grade with more manganese and less nickel (about 3.5–5.5%) — suited to indoor partitions, budget fencing and dry duty. Same openings and wire gauges; price and corrosion life differ by grade.




    What if my RFQ says SS 202 — is that the same as SS 201?
    No — AISI 201 and AISI 202 are different chemistry ranges, but Indian trade often confuses or mixes them as “200-series / economy stainless.” GARG stocks SS 201 as the economy welded-mesh grade alongside SS 304. If your BOQ literally requires true SS 202, tell us on the RFQ so we can confirm supplyability — do not assume silent substitution.




    Welded mesh vs woven wire mesh — which do I need?
    Welded mesh is rigid at every cross — better for machine guards, panels, fencing grids and cut pieces that must hold shape. Woven wire cloth / mosquito jali is interwoven and can fray when cut — better for fine filtration and insect screens. Say weld mesh or welded wire mesh when you mean this product.




    Welded mesh vs chain link fencing?
    Chain link is interlocked diamond fencing fabric in rolls. Welded mesh is a welded square/rectangular grid supplied as rolls or panels. Different product — see our GI / MS chain link mesh page for diamond jali.




    SS welded mesh vs perforated sheet — are they the same?
    No. Welded mesh is a wire grid fused at crossings. Perforated sheet is solid plate with punched holes. Different strength, open area and install. Need punched plate? See perforated sheets.




    SS welded mesh vs GI welded mesh — which should I buy?
    SS welded mesh (304 or 201) is stainless — better corrosion and cleanability for wet, hygiene-adjacent or long outdoor life. GI welded mesh is galvanized mild steel — usually lower ₹/kg for dry or coated outdoor fencing. If your drawing says stainless or SS jali, do not substitute GI without approval.




    What sizes of SS welded mesh do you supply?
    We publish 29 SKUs covering openings from 1/4 inch (6.35 mm) to 3 inch (75 mm), including rectangular meshes, with wire from about 0.81 mm (21g) to 4.06 mm (8g). Standard roll reference is 4 ft × 50 ft. Panels and cut-to-size on RFQ. Same size matrix for SS 304 and SS 201.




    Is 1 inch SS welded mesh the same as 25 mm?
    In India trade, “1 inch mesh” and “25 mm mesh” usually mean the same commercial opening (~25 × 25 mm). Always confirm clear opening vs pitch and write both inch and mm on the RFQ so the quote matches your drawing.




    How is mesh opening measured — pitch or clear?
    Confirm whether your drawing means clear opening (space between wires) or pitch (centre-to-centre). Pitch ≈ clear opening + wire diameter. Example: clear 25 mm with 2 mm wire ≈ 27 mm pitch. Open area for square mesh is roughly (A / (A + D))² × 100. Always state opening type and wire separately on the RFQ.




    Why does g/sqft × 200 give the roll weight?
    Our standard roll reference is 4 ft × 50 ft = 200 sq ft. So approximate roll kg ≈ (g per sq ft ÷ 1000) × 200. Example: 180 g/sqft → 0.18 × 200 = 36 kg per roll. Actual billed weight may vary slightly with wire tolerance and edge trim.




    Which grade for outdoor fencing in Delhi NCR?
    For long outdoor life in Delhi NCR weather we usually recommend SS 304. SS 201 can work for budget or sheltered/dry outdoor runs with shorter expected life — not a drop-in for coastal or chloride-heavy duty.




    Which grade for machine guards / food areas?
    Machine guards in dry indoor plants can use SS 201 or SS 304 by budget. Washdown, food-adjacent, dairy or hygiene-sensitive areas should specify SS 304 (or higher if your drawing says so). We do not overclaim food certification for SS 201 or for 304 without your MTC / audit requirements.

faqs.q: What is SS welded mesh / weld mesh jali?
faqs.a: SS welded mesh (weld mesh / weldmesh / stainless welded wire mesh) is stainless steel wire resistance-welded at every intersection into a rigid square or rectangular grid. In India it is also called SS jali or weld mesh jali. It is not woven mosquito mesh, not diamond chain-link, and not perforated sheet.

faqs.q: Difference between SS 304 and SS 201 welded mesh?
faqs.a: SS 304 (AISI 304 / UNS S30400) has higher nickel (about 8–10.5%) and better corrosion resistance for wet outdoor, washdown and food-adjacent work. SS 201 (AISI 201 / UNS S20100) is the economy stainless grade with more manganese and less nickel (about 3.5–5.5%) — suited to indoor partitions, budget fencing and dry duty. Same openings and wire gauges; price and corrosion life differ by grade.

faqs.q: What if my RFQ says SS 202 — is that the same as SS 201?
faqs.a: No — AISI 201 and AISI 202 are different chemistry ranges, but Indian trade often confuses or mixes them as “200-series / economy stainless.” GARG stocks SS 201 as the economy welded-mesh grade alongside SS 304. If your BOQ literally requires true SS 202, tell us on the RFQ so we can confirm supplyability — do not assume silent substitution.

faqs.q: Welded mesh vs woven wire mesh — which do I need?
faqs.a: Welded mesh is rigid at every cross — better for machine guards, panels, fencing grids and cut pieces that must hold shape. Woven wire cloth / mosquito jali is interwoven and can fray when cut — better for fine filtration and insect screens. Say weld mesh or welded wire mesh when you mean this product.

faqs.q: Welded mesh vs chain link fencing?
faqs.a: Chain link is interlocked diamond fencing fabric in rolls. Welded mesh is a welded square/rectangular grid supplied as rolls or panels. Different product — see our chain link mesh page for diamond jali.

faqs.q: SS welded mesh vs perforated sheet — are they the same?
faqs.a: No. Welded mesh is a wire grid fused at crossings. Perforated sheet is solid plate with punched holes. Different strength, open area and install. Need punched plate? See our perforated sheets page.

faqs.q: SS welded mesh vs GI welded mesh — which should I buy?
faqs.a: SS welded mesh (304 or 201) is stainless — better corrosion and cleanability for wet, hygiene-adjacent or long outdoor life. GI welded mesh is galvanized mild steel — usually lower ₹/kg for dry or coated outdoor fencing. If your drawing says stainless or SS jali, do not substitute GI without approval.

faqs.q: Is 1 inch SS welded mesh the same as 25 mm?

faqs.q: How is mesh opening measured — pitch or clear?
faqs.a: Confirm whether your drawing means clear opening (space between wires) or pitch (centre-to-centre). Pitch ≈ clear opening + wire diameter. Example: clear 25 mm with 2 mm wire ≈ 27 mm pitch. Open area for square mesh is roughly (A / (A + D))² × 100. Always state opening type and wire separately on the RFQ.

faqs.a: Our standard roll reference is 4 ft × 50 ft = 200 sq ft. So approximate roll kg ≈ (g per sq ft ÷ 1000) × 200. Example: 180 g/sqft → 0.18 × 200 = 36 kg per roll. Actual billed weight may vary slightly with wire tolerance and edge trim.
